facts.text: Littlerock, named after the Little Rock Wash, earned its nickname “The Fruit Basket of the Antelope Valley” with historic orchards of almonds, apples, peaches, and pears.
Founded in 1893, Littlerock grew into an agricultural hub of about 12,600 residents, nestled in the San Gabriel Mountains foothills roughly 50 miles north of Los Angeles.
The 1924 Littlerock Dam, a historic architectural landmark, still supplies irrigation water to orchards and offers boating, fishing, and camping on its reservoir.
Public transit in Littlerock is operated by the Antelope Valley Transit Authority, connecting residents to nearby cities.
Littlerock celebrated its first schoolhouse opening in 1913 and the founding of its first library a year later in 1914.
Littlerock lies 11 miles southeast of Palmdale’s Civic Center, bordered by Palmdale, Pearblossom, Sun Village, and the San Gabriel Mountains.
